subject: general
question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 4 hours and 32 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 4 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-fourth of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = **Filling rate** − **Emptying rate**

Total Capacity = **LCM**(4, 32, 4) = 32 units

Efficiencies: A = 8, B = 1, C = −8. Net = 8 + 1 − 8 = 1 unit/hr

One-fourth work = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 units

Time = 8 ÷ 1 = 8 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time Tap A = 4 hours, Tap B = 32 hours, Emptying time Tap C = 4 hours.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = LCM of time; Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

⇒ Net efficiency when all are open = 8 + 1 − 8 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Target volume to fill = 1/4 × Total Capacity

⇒ Target volume = 1/4 × 32 = 8 units

⇒ Time required = Target volume ÷ Net efficiency = 8 ÷ 1 = 8 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes fill the tank (positive efficiency) while outlet pipes empty it (negative efficiency).

LCM Method for Capacity

Assuming the cistern capacity as the LCM of individual time periods simplifies fractional calculations.

Net Rate Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours, the net work in 1 hour is (1/x − 1/y).</p
